rules.title: An AI data schema is explicitly defined for every in-scope semantic model
rules.requirement: Every semantic model exposed to Copilot or bound to a data agent must have an AI data schema defined through Prep data for AI, rather than defaulting to the full model surface.
rules.rationale: This is the primary control against the ad-hoc-SQL-server behaviour. The DAX generation tool uses only the AI data schema. If you never define one, the generator reasons over everything you own.

check.how: Inspect the model's LSDL / AI data schema definition. Confirm a curated selection exists and is narrower than the full object list.
check.expected: defined and narrower than full model

rules.remediation: Open Prep data for AI > Simplify the data schema and deselect every field not required by the intended question set.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator considers every table, column and measure on every question - maximum latency, maximum token cost, maximum ambiguity.

rules.title: Model entity count stays within the 1,000-entity indexing ceiling
rules.requirement: The combined count of tables and columns in the model should stay at or below 1,000 entities, or the AI data schema must reduce the exposed surface to below that ceiling.
rules.rationale: Power BI indexes a maximum of 1,000 model entities (tables and columns combined) for instance-value search. Beyond that, columns go unindexed and value-based filtering silently degrades.

check.how: Count tables plus columns via INFO.TABLES()/INFO.COLUMNS() or a VPAX extract. Compare against 1000.

rules.remediation: Trim the model, or narrow the AI data schema so the AI-visible entity count is well under the ceiling. Aim materially below 1,000, not at it.
rules.impactIfViolated: Columns are skipped during indexing; Copilot cannot resolve filter values it should be able to find.

limit.description: Maximum model entities indexed for instance values.

rules.title: Instance-value indexing stays within the 5 million value ceiling
rules.requirement: The total indexed instance values across the model must stay under 5 million, and high-cardinality columns must be excluded from the AI data schema where they are not needed for filtering.
rules.rationale: Indexing stops at 5 million instance values. When the next column would push the total over, Power BI skips that column entirely - and it may be a column that matters. A single high-cardinality key can consume the budget and starve every column after it.

check.how: Estimate distinct-value counts per AI-visible column (APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT or COLUMNSTATISTICS) and sum. Compare against 5,000,000.

rules.remediation: Deselect surrogate keys, GUIDs, free-text notes and transaction identifiers from the AI data schema. Keep the columns users actually name in questions.
rules.impactIfViolated: Arbitrary columns silently unindexed; value filters fail unpredictably and look like model bugs.

limit.description: Upper bound on indexed instance values; a column that would exceed it is skipped entirely.

rules.title: Filterable text values are under 100 characters
rules.requirement: Columns intended for value-based filtering by Copilot must contain values shorter than 100 characters.
rules.rationale: Text values of 100 characters or more are not indexed. Long descriptive strings will never be matched by a user's natural-language filter no matter how the question is phrased.

check.how: For each AI-visible text column, compute MAX(LEN(column)). Flag any column used for filtering whose values reach 100 characters.

rules.remediation: Split long text into a short filterable code or category column plus a long descriptive column, and expose only the short one to the AI data schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Users filter on a value that visibly exists in the report and Copilot insists it cannot find it.

limit.description: Text values at or above this length are not indexed.

rules.title: Copilot Diagnostics shows no AgentSchemaReduced warning
rules.requirement: Copilot Diagnostics must not report 'AgentSchemaReduced' for in-scope models under representative questions.
rules.rationale: AgentSchemaReduced means the schema was too large for Copilot to render and Copilot automatically cut it down - by its own choice, not yours. Whatever it dropped is invisible to the generator and you did not decide what went.

check.how: Run the golden question set and inspect Copilot Diagnostics warnings for AgentSchemaReduced.

rules.remediation: Reduce the AI data schema yourself until the warning clears, so schema reduction is a deliberate curation decision rather than an automatic truncation.
rules.impactIfViolated: Silent, uncontrolled loss of schema; answers omit data that exists and nobody can explain why.

rules.title: Surrogate keys and relationship identifiers are removed from the AI schema
rules.requirement: Unique identifier columns used only to define relationships must be deselected from the AI data schema.
rules.rationale: Documented explicitly as a field type to deselect. Keys carry no business meaning, add cardinality against the indexing budget, and invite the generator to join or group on them.

check.how: List AI-visible columns whose names match key patterns (ID, Key, SK, GUID, Code suffixes) and confirm exclusion unless deliberately kept.

rules.remediation: Deselect them in Simplify the data schema. Relationships still work; the generator just stops seeing the keys.
rules.impactIfViolated: Grouping by meaningless identifiers, wasted index budget, and joins the generator invents rather than follows.

rules.title: Sort-order and helper columns are removed from the AI schema
rules.requirement: Sort-by columns such as Month (Sort Order) or Day (Sort Order), and other presentation helper columns, must be deselected from the AI data schema.
rules.rationale: Called out explicitly as fields to deselect. They duplicate a real attribute in numeric form, so the generator has two plausible columns for one concept and picks wrong roughly half the time.

check.how: Identify columns used as Sort By Column targets and confirm they are excluded from the AI schema.

rules.remediation: Deselect all sort-order columns. Sorting behaviour in visuals is unaffected.
rules.impactIfViolated: Answers grouped by 1..12 instead of month names; user trust erodes on cosmetic-looking errors.

rules.title: Archived, staging and audit tables are excluded
rules.requirement: Archived, staging, audit and unrelated tables must be excluded from both the AI data schema and any data agent object selection.
rules.rationale: Explicit guidance for data agent configuration: select only the tables, columns, views and functions needed for the intended questions. Staging tables are the classic source of near-duplicate results.

check.how: Review the AI-visible table list against the intended question set; flag any table that no in-scope question needs.

rules.remediation: Remove them from selection. If they must stay in the model for lineage, hide them and exclude them from the AI schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator queries a staging copy and returns numbers that do not tie to any published report.

rules.title: AI data schema is scoped to a declared question set
rules.requirement: Each AI data schema must be traceable to a written statement of the question scope the model is meant to serve, and every included object must be justified by at least one question in that scope.
rules.rationale: 'Select only relevant objects based on the data agent's question scope to reduce ambiguity and latency.' Without a declared scope, inclusion decisions are arbitrary and the schema only ever grows.

check.how: Confirm a question-scope document exists per model/agent and that schema inclusions map to it.

rules.remediation: Write the scope statement first, derive the schema from it, and reject additions that no scoped question requires.
rules.impactIfViolated: Schema sprawl returns within two release cycles and undoes every other tuning effort.

rules.title: Data agent object selection matches the model's AI data schema
rules.requirement: For a semantic model bound to a data agent, the tables selected in the data agent must be the same tables defined in the model's Prep for AI AI data schema.
rules.rationale: Stated as a direct consistency rule. Divergence means the agent exposes objects the DAX generator was never configured to reason about.

check.how: Diff the agent's selected object list against the model's AI data schema. The sets must match.

rules.remediation: Reconcile the two selections and add a check to the release process so they cannot drift.
rules.impactIfViolated: Objects visible to the agent but absent from the generation schema produce failed or nonsensical DAX.

rules.title: Dependent objects of selected measures are included in the schema
rules.requirement: When a measure is included in the AI data schema, every object it depends on must also be included.
rules.rationale: Explicit dependency rule; Semantic Link Labs' get_measure_dependencies is the recommended way to enumerate them. A measure whose dependencies were trimmed away fails at query time.

check.how: Run get_measure_dependencies (Semantic Link Labs) across AI-visible measures and confirm every dependency is also AI-visible.

rules.remediation: Add the missing dependencies, or drop the measure from the schema if its dependencies must stay hidden.
rules.impactIfViolated: Generated DAX references objects the generator believes exist and the query errors.

rules.title: Hidden fields are not silently relied upon
rules.requirement: Any field that Copilot must be able to use has to be visible; hidden measures and columns are excluded from grounding and must not appear in verified answers.
rules.rationale: Hidden fields are excluded from grounding data, and verified answers referencing hidden columns simply do not work. Teams routinely hide a column for report tidiness and then wonder why Copilot cannot answer about it.

check.how: List objects referenced by verified answers and by the question scope, and confirm none are hidden.
check.expected: no hidden objects in AI scope

rules.remediation: Unhide the fields Copilot needs, or rewrite the verified answer against visible equivalents.
rules.impactIfViolated: Verified answers fail silently and Copilot claims data it can see in reports does not exist.

rules.title: Private tables are understood to be entirely invisible to Copilot
rules.requirement: Tables marked private must be documented as fully excluded from all Copilot grounding, and no AI capability may depend on them.
rules.rationale: Copilot ignores private tables entirely across both the data-question and DAX query view paths. This is a useful deliberate exclusion mechanism, but a trap when unintentional.

check.how: List tables marked private and confirm no in-scope question depends on them.

rules.remediation: Use the private flag deliberately to fence off sensitive or technical tables; unmark any table Copilot legitimately needs.
rules.impactIfViolated: Unexplainable gaps in Copilot's knowledge of the model.

rules.title: Duplicate field names across tables are eliminated or disambiguated
rules.requirement: The AI-visible schema must not contain identically named fields in multiple tables unless each carries a description that distinguishes it.
rules.rationale: Called out directly: 'Name' in a Customer table versus a Store table forces the generator to guess. Ambiguity at schema level cannot be recovered by a better prompt.

check.how: Group AI-visible column and measure names; flag any name appearing in more than one table.

rules.remediation: Rename to Customer Name / Store Name, or add distinguishing descriptions to each.
rules.impactIfViolated: Roughly random field selection on any question naming the ambiguous term.

rules.title: Instance-value reindexing cadence is understood and accounted for
rules.requirement: The team must document the reindexing behaviour that applies to each model type and set user expectations accordingly.
rules.rationale: Import models reindex on manual or scheduled refresh, but only when Copilot or Q&A has been used in the last 14 days. DirectQuery and Direct Lake reindex when the index is older than 24 hours under the same 14-day activity condition, with COLUMNSTATISTICS cached for 7 days. A model nobody has asked a question of for two weeks stops being reindexed.

check.how: Confirm the operations runbook records the reindexing rules per model type and the 14-day activity dependency.

rules.remediation: Document it, and for low-traffic but important models schedule a periodic synthetic question to keep the model within the activity window.
rules.impactIfViolated: Stale instance values produce filter misses that look like data errors.

rules.title: DirectQuery indexing constraints are accepted or mitigated
rules.requirement: For DirectQuery models, confirm the source supports APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT and accept that indexing occurs at most once per 24 hours unless the model is republished.
rules.rationale: Only columns from sources supporting APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT are indexed at all. A failed underlying refresh leaves a stale index until the next successful one.

check.how: For each DirectQuery model, record source support for APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT and the observed index age.

rules.remediation: Where the source does not support it, consider Import or Direct Lake for the AI-facing model.
rules.impactIfViolated: Value filtering effectively unavailable on DirectQuery models against unsupported sources.

rules.title: Prep for AI changes are given time to propagate before re-testing
rules.requirement: Test cycles must allow up to 24 hours for Prep for AI changes to affect Copilot results, typically within an hour, with the longer tail on models that have many attached reports.
rules.rationale: Re-testing five minutes after a change and concluding the change did nothing leads to thrashing the configuration.

check.how: Confirm the test procedure documents the propagation window.

rules.remediation: Build the wait into the evaluation cadence; batch configuration changes rather than tuning one setting at a time.
rules.impactIfViolated: Configuration churn and false conclusions about which settings help.

limit.description: Maximum propagation time for Prep for AI changes; usually within one hour.

rules.title: Prep for AI edits deployed via Git or pipelines are followed by a refresh
rules.requirement: After deploying LSDL or Prep for AI changes through Git integration or deployment pipelines, the model must be refreshed in the Power BI service to sync the changes.
rules.rationale: Explicit requirement. Import models must be refreshed; DirectQuery and Direct Lake models must be refreshed but only once a day. Skipping this leaves production running the previous AI configuration while source control says otherwise.

check.how: Confirm the deployment pipeline includes a post-deployment refresh step for AI-configured models.

rules.remediation: Add the refresh to the release pipeline and verify the AI configuration post-deployment rather than assuming it landed.
rules.impactIfViolated: Deployed AI configuration silently inactive in production.

rules.title: Connection type is supported for Desktop-based Prep for AI authoring
rules.requirement: Where Prep for AI is authored in Power BI Desktop, the model must use Import, DirectQuery or local Composite mode.
rules.rationale: Power BI Desktop supports only those connection types for Prep data for AI. All model types can use the features in the Power BI service, so the constraint is on where you author, not where you consume.

check.how: Record the connection type of each model and where its AI configuration is authored.

rules.remediation: Author Prep for AI in the service for model types Desktop does not support.
rules.impactIfViolated: Prep for AI unavailable in Desktop and the team assumes the feature is broken.

rules.title: Data agent stays within the five data source limit and uses the minimum needed
rules.requirement: A data agent must be bound to no more than five data sources, and to the fewest sources that its question scope actually requires.
rules.rationale: Five sources is a hard cap in any combination across Lakehouses, Warehouses, semantic models, KQL databases, mirrored databases, ontologies and Microsoft Graph. Every additional source widens the routing decision the agent has to make on every question.

check.how: Count bound data sources per agent and compare against the intended question scope.

rules.remediation: Split broad agents into several narrowly scoped agents rather than binding more sources to one.
rules.impactIfViolated: At the cap, source routing errors dominate; beyond it, configuration is rejected.

rules.title: Lakehouse content is exposed as tables, not files
rules.requirement: Data intended for agent consumption from a Lakehouse must be registered as tables; standalone files are not accessible.
rules.rationale: Agents access only Lakehouse tables, not standalone CSV or JSON files unless those are ingested as tables. Unstructured formats such as .pdf, .docx and .txt are unsupported outright.

check.how: For each Lakehouse source, confirm the required data is registered as tables.

rules.remediation: Ingest the files as Delta tables before binding the Lakehouse to the agent.
rules.impactIfViolated: The agent cannot see data the user can see in OneLake.
